question: BASE_RUNTIME_MAXIMIZED requires knowing why the runtime sits ~2,000x below its memory-bandwidth roofline. Memoizing verification recovered 2.55x. What accounts for the rest?
answer: Roughly 1,171 full CPU-to-GPU synchronizations per decode token. Every matvec and every batched expert group creates its own command buffer and calls commit_and_wait, draining the pipeline before the next one is encoded.
source_confirmation: gravity_glm.rs:1253 documents the batch path as 'one TokenCommandBuffer, one commit_and_wait for the whole batch' -- correct for a batch, but there are three such batches per MoE layer plus twelve individual matvecs.
gravity_glm.rs:1294 is the commit_and_wait for the batched path.
The singular dispatch reads y_buf.contents() immediately after dispatch, which requires the same synchronous completion.
gravity_glm.rs:496,497,506 issue THREE separate matvec_batch calls per MoE layer -- gates, ups, downs -- so even the batched path drains the pipeline three times per layer.
gravity_glm.rs:587,593,597,604,691 are five individual attention matvecs per layer, each its own round trip.
why_this_is_the_dominant_term_and_not_a_: 2.58 GB of active weights at ~800 GB/s is 3.2 ms of real memory work per token. The token takes 6,446 ms. Nothing about the codec, the expert count or the artifact size explains a 2,000x gap; ~1,171 pipeline drains at ~5.5 ms each explains essentially all of it. The GPU is idle for most of every token, waiting for the CPU to encode the next single dispatch.

what_this_means_for_the_targets.if_the_sync_count_stays: 50 tok/s would require each of the 1,171 synchronizations to cost 17.1 us, which is below plausible command-buffer submit-and-wait latency. The target is UNREACHABLE without reducing the count.
what_this_means_for_the_targets.therefore: The gate's optimization order is correct and its items 7-9 are the load-bearing ones -- asynchronous encode/execute overlap, command-buffer collapse, and one replayable token graph. Kernel-level tuning cannot reach the target while the pipeline drains 1,171 times per token.

prior_art_in_this_campaign_that_now_read: A sealed negative records an 8-layer fused megakernel measuring 4.4x SLOWER. That was kernel FUSION -- merging the work itself -- and is not the same lever. Command-buffer collapse keeps the existing kernels and stops draining between them.
A prior decode-gap study concluded per-dispatch overhead is 'won by elimination -> ICB' (indirect command buffers). That conclusion was reached on a different model and is directly applicable here.

measured_progress_so_far.after_verification_memoization: ~0.3949 (in flight, 96.9 percent of the no-hash ceiling)

not_evidence_of: that collapsing command buffers achieves the target -- nothing has been rebuilt; this identifies where the time goes, not that it can be removed
